entries.summary: HostExecutionCore.cancel returns an object instead of void (#2004); update callers requiring Promise<void>. Its result and BotCollaboration.cancelTurn/cancelHostIntent/abortSwitch retain wakePending: true for wake-only failure and add drainError?: unknown for other post-commit failures (#2072, #2144). cancelHostIntent callers move post-commit failure handling from catch to the resolved HostIntentCancelResult, including later process failures. Its cancelled result confirms a committed cancel; conclusion can be absent until a later successful drain settles it. Replay after drain/recovery to read already_settled with the conclusion, or cancel_pending while a submitted intent awaits its terminal. The coalesced drain can fail on other Host work. Check property presence, report the unchanged rejection (the whole AggregateError for mixed failures), and retry pending work through drain/recovery, not the committed operation. cancelTurn and cancelHostIntent retain the first non-wake failure even if a later pass succeeds. Explicit drains and pre-commit failures still reject; job/outbox retry state is unchanged. See committed-cancel-wake-pending for WakeDispatchError and bot-collaboration-cancel-host-intents for the additional BotCollaboration cancellation API.
The client root exports the StoreCompatibility type used by bot-collaboration ledger inspection, so strict package installations can resolve the published declaration.
Host adapters can compute the instruction frozen by K8 sync with botTurnInstruction on the host-kit entry, using an options object and InstructionLimits.

Store lease and gate release failures preserve a refused ServiceInstallationError and its code, with the refusal and all release failures in its AggregateError cause; Hosts that matched the 0.42.0 AggregateError on first install must read cause instead. The code follows the outcome (#2010): a call that leaves its receipt pending or its stores unrestored throws upgrade_pending with every failure in its cause, so the Host runs recover(), first restarting the Host process if a stuck lease makes it fail with store_busy; a preparation error that is not the SDK's own is the new store_preparation_failed with the original error as its cause. The same type gains install_root_foreign_owner (#2001): every ServiceInstallation operation holds an install-root gate, so a second operation on one install root fails at once with lifecycle_owner_busy, and an install root owned by another user is refused before anything changes. The receipt commit protocol (#2011) adds receipt_upgrade_required, receipt_state_inconsistent, switch_unhealthy, repair_interrupted and service_program_not_current (see service-upgrade-receipt-v2), and store_overlaps_service_state: a precheck store that is, holds or lies in the install root or a daemon store's service/ directory, after resolving links and without case on darwin and win32, is refused before it is snapshotted.

upgrade-receipt.json is version 2 (#2011): ServiceUpgradeReceipt.version is 2 and a pending receipt carries kind (upgrade, rollback or repair). recover() acts on the kind, the code and where current points, starting a present current as it is instead of restoring the snapshot over its writes; a candidate found unhealthy is failed with switch_unhealthy and nothing starts, and an interrupted same-version reinstall is repair_interrupted. A pending version 1 receipt is receipt_upgrade_required: run recover() with SDK 0.42 before upgrading the SDK; a final one reads as version 2 and the next write stores version 2. Hosts that parse the receipt accept version 2 and kind; Hosts that switch on codes handle the five new ServiceInstallationErrorCode values. createServiceInstallation refuses a program that does not run from current, and upgrade() and rollback() a unit the SDK did not write, with service_program_not_current.

macOS Keychain and Linux Secret Service report an SDK entry that does not decode as the new KEYCHAIN_SECRET_CORRUPTED instead of KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED, and ProviderRegistry.replaceSecret/configure overwrite it with a new key. KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED now means an entry the SDK did not write; the registry never overwrites it and refuses before any write. A Host that offered 'enter the key again' for KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED offers it for KEYCHAIN_SECRET_CORRUPTED and shows delete, rename or other-profile guidance for KEYCHAIN_SECRET_DECODE_FAILED. ProviderRegistry.configure/replaceSecret/setDefaultModelProvider/delete reject with the new PROVIDER_CHANGE_COMMITTED when the change committed but a later step (the auth-none key delete, an unconfirmed profile-store write or the lock release) failed; treat it as success and read the status again. ProviderRegistry.configure without a secret reuses the stored key only for an authenticating profile with an unchanged base_url and otherwise rejects with PROVIDER_SECRET_MISSING.

cancelHostIntents atomically cancels selected unsubmitted Host intents without a pass. HostIntentError.rejected lists all refused keys and code gains inflight; update exhaustive switches. Existing cancelHostIntent, drainForSwitch and abortSwitch retain their other behavior, and the store format is unchanged; see committed-cancel-wake-pending for the wake-dispatch change. Hosts may replace freeze, individual cancels and abort with this call, retaining freeze when other device work must be held. Successors wait for a later pass or an explicit drain().

The local bot-collaboration entry exports inspectLedger(path, tenant), a read-only precheck returning StoreCompatibility. It reports migration-required for would-do rows without turnId; run migrateWouldDo after snapshot and before serving. LocalStoreId gains bot-collaboration-ledger; Hosts with exhaustive switches or Record<LocalStoreId, ...> must add this member.

Custom LocalTaskJournal implementations must accept the new cutoff argument of pruneConfirmedJournalTask(taskId, cutoff) (#1990) and recheck it in the delete transaction under the write lock. It returns false and deletes nothing when the task is valid but not prunable: a confirmed terminal last updated at or after cutoff, or a received offer whose first stored task.cancel sequenced above the offer was committed at or after cutoff (including evidence replaced under the same task id) or that has no such cancellation. For a received offer it throws and deletes nothing when the task.cancel that qualifies it fails its hash or enrollment check, names another task id, or carries a seq different from its row's. A confirmed terminal's envelopes, withheld rows and the task's other envelopes are not verified before deletion. An implementation that ignores cutoff still compiles but can delete unexpired or replaced evidence; the SDK does not repeat these checks.

A path mutation gate release that fails while another error is thrown is kept: PathMutationGateBusyError, ServiceUnitError and LocalStateRelocation errors keep their class and code with an AggregateError of the original error and the release failures in cause, and an error of another class from a managed service lifecycle operation becomes that AggregateError. ServiceUnitError and the LocalStateRelocation error classes accept ErrorOptions. Hosts that read the original error of such a failure read it from cause.

ServiceUnitErrorCode gains service_command_timeout (#1971): a platform command a service lifecycle or installation ran (launchctl, systemctl --user, WinSW, sc.exe, the Windows Startup launcher query and launch, the Host's Windows stop program, or icacls when a ServiceInstallation leases a store on Windows) outlived its fixed bound and was stopped, where the operation could hang before. Where it is reported: every ServiceInstallation operation's restore of an earlier install's repair snapshot (when current is absent) is upgrade_pending on a timed-out stop or lease; install() throws a timed-out stop or store lease before anything is installed as is, and a timed-out activation, start or cleanup removal is install_health_check_failed with it in cause (upgrade_pending when cleanup cannot restore the stores); a same-version reinstall throws a timed-out stop as is and keeps its pending repair receipt; upgrade() is upgrade_pending on a timed-out stop or lease before the switch, health_check_failed with it in cause on a timed-out candidate start (upgrade_pending when the rollback's stop or lease times out too), and keeps a store refusal's code when the restart of the previous version times out; rollback() throws a timed-out stop or lease as is but resolves with a failed rollback_unhealthy receipt on a timed-out start; recover() is upgrade_pending on a timed-out stop or lease before a restore but resolves with a failed receipt on a timed-out start; uninstall() throws a timed-out stop, unregistration or daemon-reload as is; the lifecycle's own operations reject with it as is. The service's state is then unknown, never "the change did not happen". ServiceUnitError gains exitConfirmed, set only with this code: true when the command is proven to have exited, false when it may still run and change the service, so a retry can race it. An exhaustive switch over ServiceUnitErrorCode needs the new case.

clearDeviceEnrollment and Daemon.unpair() no longer delete another store's credential or staged first pairing under the same productId: they hold a per-user productId lock from validation through deletion, and pairing takes it across its credential writes, each waiting up to 30 seconds. FirstPairingAttempt gains storeIdentity (DeviceStore.identity, the SHA-256 hex of the resolved storeDir); an injected DeviceCredentialBackend keeps every attempt field, or the store's own attempt is refused. A clear refuses another store's attempt as store_not_bound and an attempt that names no store (staged by 0.42.0) with the new DeviceEnrollmentClearErrorCode pairing_attempt_unattributed; clearDeviceEnrollment({ ..., clearUnattributedAttempt: true }) deletes it. Pairing applies the same rule (#2033): it reuses only its own store's staged attempt and otherwise throws the new FirstPairingAttemptRefusedError (store_not_bound, which replaceOtherStore discards, or pairing_attempt_unattributed). A running daemon's token renewal takes the same lock around its write and writes only while the OS entry still holds its store's enrollment; otherwise the daemon halts as store_not_bound or re_pair_required (#2034). A renewal never holds the lock across a network request. A pairing is one critical section: it rereads the enrollment and staged attempt under the lock, never a cached record, refuses another store's or an unattributed attempt even beside its own enrollment, and holds the lock across its own request, because server registration has no fencing, and through its E2EE member entries. A running daemon's member resume and KEM rotation write the member entries only under the same lock while its enrollment still holds, otherwise they write nothing and the daemon halts the same way (#2055). BlobClient and InstallSkillPacksOptions change only through the types they reference (#1964).

maxRetainedBytes (default 16 MiB) bounds only native and tool payloads: past it the oldest are elided in place and the task keeps running; it also covers runtime request and reply native payloads. Text and reasoning are kept whole because the folds read them, so it is not a bound on total retained bytes (#2056). For Claude this is the existing behavior (since #1892). For Codex, Grok, Antigravity, OpenCode and dsh it changes: their text used to count toward the 16 MiB total and passing it failed the task ('<runtime> retained record byte budget exceeded'); that failure no longer occurs and their text has no byte bound. ClaudeAdapterOptions gains maxRetainedBytes. A task's text grows with the provider's per-turn output limit times the number of turns; a Host that needs a hard bound sets maxDurationMs (the offer's limits.maxDurationMs, or DaemonConfig.defaultMaxDurationMs).

Move resolveHostLayout, HostLayoutInputError, HostLayout, HostLayoutOptions and HostLayoutPlatform imports from @byok-sdk/client to @byok-sdk/client/host-layout, including type-only imports. Split mixed imports and leave other symbols at the root. The new pure entry avoids loading Pi and provider SDKs in a shell or installer; paths, error codes and existing stores are unchanged (#1925).

HostExecutionCore.cancel returns an object; BotCollaboration.cancelTurn and abortSwitch may return wakePending: true when wake dispatch fails after commit. The durable outbox records lastError and retries; drain and wake hooks still reject WakeDispatchError, an AggregateError. Update callers expecting cancel to return void. See committed-cancel-drain-error for these methods and their drainError result on other post-commit failures (#2072).
@byok-sdk/cloud-do is archived after 0.42.0 and leaves the release train. Remove the dependency or pin it to exactly 0.42.0; no later fixes will be published and its npm versions will be deprecated.
